label: second copy step (step L+1) of very short sequences (L=3, weaker L=4)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only at recall_idx == 1 (the step right after <DEL>, where the input is original token 0 and the output is original token 1), and only for short sequences: L=3 holds 70% of activation mass (11% of L=3 sequences counted on all dev steps; about 68% precision at this step), L=4 holds 29% (about 11% of L=4 sequences fire), L=5 almost none, L>=6 never. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases or at any other recall position. Magnitude and firing probability depend on token identity: highest when the fed-back first token is r/x/f/o/e/c and the next output (orig(1)) is k/2/v/u/w/3/p/t; a token-set refinement reaches dev F1 0.64 / mass recall 0.81, but the token lists are ad hoc. Rarer when original tokens repeat or the sequence has several digits. Simple predicate dev: P 0.68 R 0.52 F1 0.59 mass 0.70; (recall_idx==1)&(L<=4) gets mass recall 0.998 but precision 0.20.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=5: r, x, e, o; t=6: x, r, f, e; t=4: r, c, x, e) and the next token to output (most: k, u, 2, v, 3, w; least: r, f, 0, x); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, recall_idx=1, L=3.
